newsitem.title: USA: Child abuse rates soar in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Child abuse rates soar in U.S.

text.p: The numbers of American children suffering from abuse, neglect and serious injury soared in recent years while child protection efforts lagged, according to a federal survey released on Wednesday.

From 1986-93, the number of abused and neglected children doubled, from 1.4 million to 2.8 million. And those who were seriously injured increased fourfold from about 143,000 to nearly 570,000, the third National Incident Study of Child Abuse and Neglect said.
The toll of sexual abuse rose from 133,600 to 300,200 -- a 125 percent incrase.

Children were at risk from age three and, as previous research had found, girls were the target much more often than boys, according to the study commissioned by the Department of Health and Human Services.

"It is shameful and startling to see that so many more children are in danger and that proportionately fewer incidents are investigated," Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala said in a statement.

The study did not find different rates among racial or ethnic groups, but poverty was a big risk factor, as was being in a single-parent family. Children from families with an annual income under $15,000 were 22 times more likely to experience maltreatment than those whose income was about $30,000, and were also at much higher risk for sexual abuse and serious injury.
Similarly, those from single-parent families had an 87 percent greater chance of being harmed by physical neglect, and an 80 percent greater chance of suffering serious injury.
